quest_use: The province's attested western exit. A cart or a beast of burden crosses only on this ferry, so the poler can shut the road to wagons.
why: Claywater Station's Argonian landing sits on the ford's north bank. Its poler lives beside the crossing. The ford is knee-deep and stony. The light-footed wade it. The poler takes carts, beasts and anyone who will not wade over on the plank ferry. A cart has no other way onto the Blackwood Road out of the province, so the fare is steep.

quest_use: Blackrose is a prison. The refusal predicate is the escape problem stated in data.
why: The five lake stations already declare `ferry` in `travelStation.modes` and already name each other as destinations. This edge only writes down the network they imply, so the travel system reads one graph. On a prison lake, a ferry checks who boards.

Bramman River Ferry is a road crossing the catalogue already solved: 'the coast road crosses the river south of Soulrest where it is too deep to bridge'. It pairs with the Oliis stage; the Oliis ferry 'is older than the rebuilt city'. Recorded as a station run because both ends are catalogued stations, not bare landings.

Archon and Soulrest are two of the three major seaports (Lore:Sea Transportation) and both already declare `ferry`. The long open-water leg is the one run in the province that a storm can stop, which the refusal predicate exists to cover.
retired_why: No lane exists: `route.boat.archon-estuary` was never published; both stages were unsited. Archon rides `route.boat.lilmoth-archon`.

Deliberately unreachable-by-road deep-marsh points — the network bypasses surface danger for those granted access.
